meaning.evidence: Otherwise the original, but two swaps damage it: "The Committee underlined its continuing swear blind to achieve its dual-mandate goals" loses "resolve" in a broken phrase, and "The Federal Open Market Committee reckoned the following statement was a goer for release by a 12–0 vote" turns a formal approval inside a quoted statement into an opinion.

sense.evidence: The swaps take the wrong sense: "its continuing swear blind" (resolve as a noun rendered by a verb phrase meaning to insist something is true), "reckoned the following statement was a goer" for approved; only "give a 1/4 percentage point increase the nod" fits, and even that is misplaced.

authenticity.evidence: No Australian would say "its continuing swear blind to achieve"; the rest is the US original unchanged: "Members noted that the unemployment rate was largely unchanged".

register.evidence: Largely untranslated for a level-4 brief: "At the conclusion of the discussion, the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise".

tone.evidence: The formal tone holds where untouched, but the swaps make it accidentally comic and alter a quoted official statement: "reckoned the following statement was a goer".

flow.evidence: Broken grammar where the swaps land: "underlined its continuing swear blind to achieve", "voted unanimously to give a 1/4 percentage point increase the nod in the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent".

variety.evidence: Only three one-off substitutions: "swear blind", "a goer", "the nod".

essence.evidence: Still recognisably the FOMC minutes, directive and vote intact: "Voting against this action: None."

A.summary: Barely translated, and its few swaps take the wrong sense, breaking one sentence and altering a quoted statement.

meaning.evidence: Every fact kept: the 1/4 point rise "to 3-3/4 to 4 percent", ample reserves, unemployment that "had hardly budged", the directive and statement quoted "word for word", the 12 voters, "3.90 percent", the next meeting and adjournment, the notation vote. Asides react to the original: "Not \"hope to\", mind.", "Not a peep.", "well before smoko". "a fair way above the Committee's 2 percent goal" slightly overstates "elevated relative to".

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "every last member agreed to whack the target range for the federal funds rate up 1/4 percentage point", "they stuck by the FOMC's policy", "not mucking about", "gave the nod", "They've pencilled in the Committee's next get-together", "knocked off at 10:15 a.m.".

authenticity.evidence: A real Australian telling ("here's how it went down at the Yanks' version of the RBA board", "Who put their hand up for it:"), with a couple of stock or slightly off lines: "No word of a lie", "domestic spending holding up like a champion".

register.evidence: A full level-4 retelling of the narrative, with the quoted directive and statement rightly kept verbatim and flagged: "Here it is, word for word:". No swearing, within the dial.

tone.evidence: The voice change is what the brief asks; the facts stay sober, though some jokes lean flippant on an official record: "The whole box and dice.", "well before smoko".

flow.evidence: Reads well aloud: "Once they'd talked it all out, the Committee voted to tell the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until it hears otherwise". The tags after lists clunk a little: "Christopher J. Waller. The whole box and dice."

variety.evidence: Varied: "whack", "stuck by", "hardly budged", "solid clip", "not mucking about", "gave the nod", "bump", "pencilled in", "knocked off", "smoko", "signed off".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the FOMC minutes, retold, with the directive and statement intact and the "will deliver price stability" resolve given its weight: "Not \"hope to\", mind."

B.summary: A full, varied, natural level-4 retelling that keeps every fact and quotes the formal texts verbatim; a few asides lean flippant.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept: "bump the target range for the federal funds rate up 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent", "inflation was still running too hot", directive and statement verbatim, "Voting against this action: Not a single bugger.", "3.90 percent", the next meeting and notation vote.

sense.evidence: Mostly exact ("dead set on hitting its dual-mandate goals", "voted as one", "gave the thumbs-up, no dissenters"), but "doubled down on the FOMC's policy" makes "reaffirmed" sound like an escalation, and "The meeting knocked off at 10:15 a.m." puts a worker's knock-off on a meeting.

authenticity.evidence: Mostly natural ("When the yakking wrapped up", "Not a single bugger."), with US "doubled down" and the slightly awkward "the whole lot of members".

register.evidence: A real retelling with swearing inside the dad dial ("Not a single bugger."), a bit lighter than B: "the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until told otherwise".

tone.evidence: Facts stay sober in a looser voice; "Not a single bugger." in the vote record tips toward flippant.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Members agreed the policy action they'd taken would help get inflation back to the Committee's 2 percent goal a bit quicker."

variety.evidence: Varied: "bump", "running too hot", "crystal clear", "dead set", "yakking", "signing off", "voted as one", "get-together", "thumbs-up"; "lift" and "voted as one" each twice.

essence.evidence: Clearly the FOMC minutes retold, structure and quoted texts intact.
